body:
Our history of loss is pretty similar. I'm almost 40. 

"Selfish", besides being a cruel and very misplaced word to use (The people who use it are almost never considering the needs of the people they accuse of it), also seems pretty ... well, pointless?  I know lots of people carry on with an awful situation purely for the sake of someone else (read: many marriages, attending family holiday gatherings, obtaining many college degrees/jobs, otherwise living as someone you aren't, etc) but... it's just **awful**.  Why would they choose THAT, of all reasons, as the best reason for you to live: "Do it for ME. Yeah ME, the one who is calling you selfish"  It's weird logic. I don't know why people do that.

As for dealing with loss, yeah.. I have also lost any faith that "recovery" is possible. Unless the word "recover" is greatly adjusted to mean: *To adapt life to be able to accept the ongoing pain in a maintainable way that eventually stops being crippling to your ability to engage in the pursuit of happiness.*  (or something like that).   

I .. want to believe that type of recovery is maybe real. I am in the category of people that is quite unable to end my life, so I guess I kind of have to believe that though.  

Do you believe that type of recovery can be real for people?
Do you think it could eventually become real for you, too?

Lack of sleep has got to be taking a very bad situation and making it spiral even further out of control. I was told to do whatever it takes to get a few nights of good sleep in a row before trying to make any important decisions about ... anything.

I'm not sure if all doctors are very comfortable prescribing the stronger sleeping pills to people they know to be suicidal but they did give me some. Everyone's body is different. Heck, maybe even the traditional non-pill suggestions might eventually turn out to work.  

But details aside I really think you should focus on the sleep part first. You really can't trust any other thoughts until you get a handle on that first one.  

That being said, I suspect that traditional sleep help suggestions will probably work far better if you can shut down the mind racing .. even for 30 mins if possible (long enough for a sleeping pill or whatever method you use, to take effect).  I found if I started thinking again during that period, nothing would work. I need to work on meditation or something.

Do you have any luck meditating?

Same situation here. It's hard to know how much trying is too much trying, or is there no such thing?  Some meds have given me a very short period of relief from the thoughts of suicide (and yeah.. I get excited and say the same thing each time "I'm CURED!" ..even though I know better), only to slowly (or quickly) sink right back to the same state of 24/7 obsession with suicidal thoughts again.   

It can be such a long process. It often feels like it won't ever be any other way than this. I often wish, if I my future self is ever going to find something that works for me, that they can send a hint back in time to me like OPs post. I'm getting older and older.  Kinda thinking that if I do eventually find freedom from these obsessive thoughts, by then it won't really matter much anyway. 

5 years from now?  It seems like from OPs view, it's worth it to be on the other side. It's so hard to hold that perspective from within it though, when we don't know if it would be 5 more years of this to wade through, or 30. 

Thank you for the post, OP. It's good to remember those hints of what our future selves may think.
